Numeric tower landed in sonic/src/sonic/numeric.ss. Fixnum and flonum only, no bignum/ratnum/complex. Tag scheme: 3 tag bits, fixnum tag 000, 64-bit word, so 61 value bits and range [-2^60, 2^60-1] = [-1152921504606846976, 1152921504606846975], which is what CUJ.md stage 8 already assumed and is also Chez's width so the hosted model shares the host's overflow boundary. Overflow documented and tested under all three controls: checked signals overflow-check with no bignum promotion; unchecked is UB and wraps two's-complement mod 2^61 with the tag surviving; proved emits unchecked code and is auditable via proved-audit, which accuses the analysis rather than the program. Flonums are IEEE binary64, one correctly rounded op per primitive, contraction never applied per D24, with a witness triple in the suite where one rounding and two differ by ~1.9x. 324 checks, 0 failures.

Primitives landed in sonic/src/sonic/prims.ss. All 33 primitives from the frozen table in lang.ss and nothing else, as a data table keyed by symbol with the control input as an argument, matching Lcore's (primcall pr c e* ...). checked runs the named check and signals a sonic-condition carrying the check name, who, and irritants; unchecked and proved emit identical code, and only proved is auditable. Bounds, type and overflow checks are separately named so they can be counted by name per D5. prims.ss deliberately does not import (sonic lang) to keep the runtime independent of the compiler's IR library; the two tables are cross-checked in both directions by the test. Every primitive nbody uses is covered, plus an end-to-end b[i*7+k] kernel asserted bit-identical under all three controls. Test: cd sonic && scheme -q --libdirs src:vendor/nanopass --script test/numeric-test.ss -> 324 checks, 0 failures.

sonic/src/sonic/alias.ss: flow-insensitive, allocation-site points-to over Lanf. Distinguishes two disjoint make-flvector sites (must-not) and refuses on every may-alias fixture: same variable against itself, escape through an unknown call, two names for one base, storage into a heap object, capture by an escaping closure, a reference returned by an opaque call. Soundness direction is the opposite of the interval domain's and is stated in the header: may is the safe answer, every default and every unhandled form lands there, must-not is only returned from a positive proof. Interprocedural step propagates actuals into the formals of a KNOWN procedure (bound once, to a lambda, used only as a call operator), which is what cqs.8 raises. 14 cases, 0 failures.

sonic/src/sonic/inline.ss: Lanf -> Lanf. Inlines a leaf call in the fixture. Five rules: known callee, size budget 12 Lanf nodes, not on the active inline stack (this is the termination proof, kept separate from the recursion rule so relaxing that one cannot make the pass diverge), not self- or mutually-recursive, and at non-tail sites exactly one tail position so the continuation is spliced rather than copied into every branch. Effects cannot be duplicated: Lanf operands are atoms, so a parameter is substituted by a variable, never by the expression that produced it. ANF invariant checked in the test by an independent walker (result still named at the call's binding, binders unique, no free variable introduced). nbody effect NOT measured and not claimed: nothing here is tuned toward it, per Waddell and Dybvig's 0.92-1.05 on the R4400. Demonstrated payoff is on cqs.7 instead: a helper called on two array pairs merges its formals and alias says may; inline it and each site's arrays are provably distinct. 21 checks, 0 failures.
